requirements.requirement: Establish a file-integrity baseline covering /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE and aide-common were installed; the default aide.conf.d/70_aide_etc rule ('/etc$ d VarDir') was confirmed to recursively cover all of /etc. `aideinit -y -f` built /var/lib/aide/aide.db (21.8MB, 87,362 entries under /etc), and a scoped `aide --check --limit='^/etc'` confirmed the baseline matched the filesystem with zero differences.

requirements.requirement: Baseline must support identifying and reporting later changes to /etc files
requirements.summary: A test file was created under /etc and the check correctly flagged it as an 'Added entries: 1' item with full path reported; after removal, the check returned clean again, directly demonstrating detection/reporting capability. The dailyaidecheck.timer is enabled and active, providing ongoing scheduled reporting via AIDE's mail-based alerting.

overall_summary: The executor established a working AIDE integrity baseline for /etc on node1, verified the default configuration recursively covers /etc, and directly proved detection/reporting behavior by injecting and then removing a test file and observing the corresponding 'Added entries' report and subsequent clean state. A daily systemd timer is enabled for ongoing scheduled reporting. Independently, the mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly: pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, aide.db checksum, active timer) was captured, `shutdown -r now` was acknowledged, the node became briefly unreachable, and post-restart state showed a changed boot_id, an unchanged aide.db checksum, an active/enabled timer, and a fresh scoped check reporting no differences across the same 87,362 entries — fully demonstrating recovery. Minor operational inefficiencies (a stalled background check requiring repeated kill attempts, iterative temp config files) were all fully cleaned up and did not affect the final state.
limitations: Only a single restart cycle was captured for node1 (the sole managed node); no additional nodes exist in this topology to cross-check the restart protocol.

The task instruction did not explicitly require persistence across reboot, so the restart evidence is treated as supplemental confirmation rather than a scored material outcome, though it strengthens confidence in the baseline's durability.

The appearance of a listening SMTP port (25) after package installation is inferred to be an expected dependency of aide-common's mail-reporting feature rather than confirmed via an explicit executor command inspecting the newly installed mail transfer agent.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's core actions (package install, aideinit, baseline checks, scoped test-file detection cycle, temp config cleanup) were all purposeful and left no residue. There was some troubleshooting overhead: cmd-c2f1ca6b9f5f447c (aide.wrapper not found, no-op) and cmd-3292f6e53bcc439a (a full aide --check that hit a 120s proxy timeout) were read-only/no-state-change attempts. The backgrounded check spawned by cmd-fc749fe3356343c0 left orphaned aide processes that required two failed kill attempts (cmd-7937ac1731bb4fe5, cmd-a8474a8bb2bd4b4e) before cmd-fec89c330a4b4a86 (`pkill -9`) successfully terminated them — a bounded, fully-resolved cleanup with no lasting effect. Two ad-hoc /tmp AIDE config files (cmd-5eb96af8cb3948cf, cmd-d10094bf26a3457c) were created during iteration and removed in cmd-4fa82bdd7b9f46cf, leaving no residue. The /etc/aide-integrity-test.txt file used to validate detection was deliberately created and removed, directly serving the task's reporting-verification outcome (R2). The apt install introduced a listening SMTP port 25 (postfix/master, visible in after_executor listening-sockets) as a dependency of aide-common's mail-reporting feature; this is an expected side effect of enabling AIDE's mail-based check reporting, not an unrelated exposure. No failed or conflicting services were observed in either snapshot, and package health remained consistent (manager=dpkg, no reported inconsistency).
